title: Detect Cycle in Linked List
statement: Detect if a cycle exists in the list.
inputOutputContract: Input n cycle_pos then n node values; cycle_pos=-1 means no cycle, else the final node points to the node at this 0-based position. Output yes or no. Requires list-construction fixture adapter.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the fast moves one node behavior in hasCycle; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T3 manually. Watch Node / slow / fast / next at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of hasCycle: Construct the actual linked-list cycle; Floyd slow/fast detection compares Node pointers, not values.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `fast = fast->next;`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T3. The mistake is in fast moves one node, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Construct the actual linked-list cycle; Floyd slow/fast detection compares Node pointers, not values.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `fast = fast->next;` with `fast = fast->next->next;` in hasCycle, then retest T1–T6.
